title: Healing and secondary displacement after palmar open-wedge osteotomy for distal radial malunion without bone graft
content:
by Robin Benjamin Kim Hansson, Miled Dhaouadi, Therese Collin, Emir Ouahrani, Hans Erik Berg, Yan Li

This retrospective cohort study assessed whether the presence or absence of cortical contact influenced healing and secondary displacement after palmar open-wedge osteotomy without bone grafting in extra-articular distal radial malunion. Seventy-nine patients treated at a single tertiary center between 1999 and 2024 were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the presence or absence of cortical contact on intraoperative fluoroscopic images. Secondary displacement and bone healing were the primary outcomes. Secondary outcomes included group analysis of cortical contact, complications and re-operations. The median radiographic follow-up duration was 28 weeks (IQR 14–60). Cortical contact was present in 38 patients, whereas 39 patients had no cortical contact. Surgical correction was generally maintained, with radiographic healing observed in 37 patients (47%) during the available follow-up period. The overall incidence of complications was low. Revision surgery for primary outcomes was required in three patients: one for nonunion and two for secondary displacement. Cortical contact was absent in the nonunion case, present in one patient with secondary displacement and not assessable in one case because of missing direct postoperative radiographs. No differences were observed between groups in radiographic alignment or healing. These findings suggest that palmar open-wedge osteotomy with anterior locking plate fixation without bone grafting may be a viable treatment option for distal radial malunion, and that loss of cortical contact may not affect healing or secondary displacement.
